title: This year, the highest fire count and Diwali fell on the same day
description: On Diwali, 8 November, satellites recorded the season's most fire detections so far, the first time since at least 2019 the two fell on the same day. Six of 13 independent sensors in Delhi passed AQI 1,000 that night; by 9 am Monday Lahore's monitors averaged 398.5 µg/m³ of PM2.5, against 219 a day earlier, while the forecast model had the city getting cleaner.
abstract: Every autumn, crop burning and Diwali fireworks foul the air of both Punjabs. On Sunday 8 November 2026 they fell on the same day: satellites recorded 5,419 fire detections across Pakistan and northern India, the season's highest so far, with Indian Punjab's count more than tripling. In no season since 2019 had the busiest fire day fallen on Diwali. At 9 am on Monday, Lahore's ground monitors averaged 398.5 µg/m³ of PM2.5 (US AQI 646), against 219 at the same hour on Sunday; all 48 monitors with readings on both mornings were higher, and two passed AQI 1,000. Multan and Faisalabad spiked the same night. The CAMS model behind many free forecasts had Lahore getting cleaner. In Delhi, six of 13 independent sensors passed AQI 1,000 on Diwali night, one reaching 2,089. Lahore's evening was quiet; its air worsened after midnight on a light east wind that had spent Diwali evening over Indian Punjab. Fire counts, weather and humidity do not explain the jump on their own, and the data cannot separate fireworks, crop fires and the cities' own pollution.
